title: A bill to amend the Federal Water Pollution Control Act to reauthorize the National Estuary Program, and for other purposes.
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was passed by the House on April 26, 2016. The summary of that version is repeated here.)

(Sec. 1) This bill amends the Federal Water Pollution Control Act (commonly known as the Clean Water Act) to revise the National Estuary Program by requiring the Environmental Protection Agency to make competitive awards to address urgent and challenging issues that threaten the economic and ecological well-being of coastal areas, including:

  • extensive seagrass habitat losses,
  • recurring harmful algae blooms,
  • unusual marine mammal mortalities,
  • invasive exotic species,
  • jellyfish proliferation limiting community access to water during peak tourism seasons,
  • flooding that may be related to sea level rise or wetland degradation or loss, and
  • low dissolved oxygen conditions in estuarine waters and related nutrient management.

(Sec. 2) The bill authorizes appropriations for FY2017-FY2021 for: (1) EPA administrative expenses relating to a grant or award, and (2) making grants and awards. The bill allocates funding for conservation and management plans for estuaries and for competitive awards.

summary.headline: A 2016 law reauthorizes the National Estuary Program under the Clean Water Act and directs EPA to make competitive awards for coastal problems.
summary.what_it_does: The law amends the Clean Water Act to update the National Estuary Program, which supports work to protect bays, sounds, and other coastal waters where rivers meet the ocean. It requires the Environmental Protection Agency to make competitive awards aimed at specific problems, such as seagrass loss, harmful algae blooms, unusual marine mammal deaths, invasive species, jellyfish crowding beaches during tourist season, flooding linked to sea level rise or wetland loss, and low oxygen in estuary water. It also authorizes funding for fiscal years 2017 through 2021 for EPA administration, grants and awards, and conservation and management plans for estuaries.

who_it_affects.group: Coastal communities and local governments near estuaries
who_it_affects.how: They may be able to compete for EPA awards aimed at the coastal problems listed in the law.

who_it_affects.group: Coastal tourism businesses and beach communities
who_it_affects.how: The law names jellyfish blooms that limit access to water during peak tourist seasons as an issue that awards may address.

who_it_affects.group: State and local estuary program partners
who_it_affects.how: The law authorizes funding for conservation and management plans for estuaries, which these partners often help carry out.

who_it_affects.group: Commercial and recreational fishing and shellfish interests
who_it_affects.how: Efforts to address seagrass loss, algae blooms, low oxygen, and marine mammal deaths may affect the health of fish and shellfish habitat.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted May 20, 2016; the funding authorizations cover fiscal years 2017 through 2021.
